answer:
In Phase 2 clinical trials, R21/Matrix-M demonstrated 77% effectiveness [2]. Phase 3 trials reported 12-month vaccine efficacy of 75% at seasonal sites [2]. The same trials reported 68% efficacy at standard sites [2]. Vaccine efficacy against multiple clinical malaria episodes was 75% at seasonal sites [2]. It was 67% at standard sites [2]. The vaccine has shown up to 77% protection against the malaria parasite in clinical trials [2].

R21/Matrix-M was well tolerated and offered high efficacy against clinical malaria in African children [3]. This low-cost, high-efficacy vaccine is already licensed by several African countries [3]. It recently received a WHO policy recommendation and prequalification [3].
